captions: Hello, and welcome to Atomic English, Stage 6. In this lesson: The year 2150.
Read a science fiction story and use future forms correctly.
Here are some new words. Science fiction. Stories about the future, space or new technology. Android.
A robot that looks like a human. Colony. A place where people from another place settle and live.
And some more words. Hover. Stay in the air in one place. Solar. Using energy from the sun. Predict.
Say what you think will happen.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: stories about the future, space or new technology?
Now some grammar: Future forms. Use will for predictions and quick decisions,
going to for plans and clear signs, and the present continuous for fixed arrangements.
For example: In 2150, cities will float. For example: We're going to visit the colony.
For example: I'm meeting Zara at 6.
Now listen, and read along. Zara's first day on Ocean Colony.
The year was 2150, and Ocean Colony floated two hundred metres below the waves.
Zara pressed her face to the thick glass window. A shoal of silver fish turned like a single shining cloud.
‘Your lessons begin in ten minutes,’ said Tik, her android helper.
‘Today you are learning how the colony makes oxygen from seawater.’ Zara sighed.
‘Tik, will I ever see the sky?’ Tik's blue eyes flickered.
‘Your family is going to visit the surface station next month. The weather forecast says it will be sunny.’
Zara smiled for the first time that day. She had never felt real sunlight on her skin.
Next month, she would.
Another question. The video will stop. Where is Ocean Colony?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like science fiction, android, colony. You practised future forms.
And you read Zara's first day on Ocean Colony. Now try the practice questions. See you next time!

sections.title: Inventing the future

captions: Hello, and welcome to Atomic English, Stage 6. In this lesson: Inventing the future.
Make predictions with modals and plan a science fiction story.
Here are some new words. Technology. Machines and tools made using science. Possibility.
Something that might happen. Probably. Almost certainly.
And some more words. Definitely. Certainly, without any doubt. Unlikely. Probably not going to happen.
Setting. Where and when a story takes place.
Time for a question. The video will stop. Which word means: machines and tools made using science?
Now some grammar: Degrees of certainty. Use will definitely, will probably, might,
probably won't and definitely won't to show how sure you are about the future.
For example: Cars will probably drive themselves. For example: People might live on the Moon.
For example: We definitely won't stop learning.
Now listen, and read along. Story planner: The last library.
Title: The last library Setting: A city in 2099 where all books are digital and paper is banned.
Main character: Omar, 12, curious and a little rebellious. He secretly loves the smell of old paper.
Problem: Omar finds a hidden room full of paper books.
The city's cleaning robots will probably destroy it if anyone finds out.
Ideas for the middle: He might share the books with his friends. Someone will definitely try to stop him.
Ending: Probably happy – the city council decides that people can choose between paper and digital books.
Another question. The video will stop. When is the story set?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like technology, possibility, probably.
You practised degrees of certainty. And you read Story planner: The last library.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!
